polityNote: First-level units of Turkmenistan from the dissolution of the USSR (26 Dec 1991) to the velayat reform of 14 Dec 1992, from which the Natural Earth fill draws. Atoms: geoBoundaries TKM ADM2 (CIESIN 2009, CC BY-SA, 59 units, 5,901 vertices; some units unnamed; a clean partition, 0 overlaps at 0.05°), grouped by the 2007 first-level layer (that layer itself, 1,322 vertices, is coarser than Natural Earth and is not used). The velayat articles say each velayat was formed on the territory of the former oblast; no transfer between them is recorded before 2009. Check ① (geodesic area of the union against the oblasts’ stated 1987 areas): Tashauz 76,429 vs 73,600 km² = 1.04; Chardzhou 96,473 vs 93,800 km² = 1.03; Mary 85,774 vs 86,800 km² = 0.99; Balkan 138,383 vs Krasnovodsk 138,500 km² = 1.00. No source states the number of first-level units for 1992, so no count is asserted. OpenHistoricalMap carries only the country for these years.

sources.title: Wikipedia (ru) — Ташаузская область (oldid 151440953)
sources.says: Tashauz oblast existed 1939–1963 and 1970–1992; Darganata district went to Chardzhou in 1944; on 14 Dec 1992 Dashhowuz (Dashoguz) velayat was formed on its territory. 1987 area 73.6 thousand km².

sources.title: Wikipedia (ru) — Дашогузский велаят (oldid 154388011)

sources.title: Statoids — Provinces of Turkmenistan, change history
sources.says: Gives 1991-10-27 for the change of province names to Ahal, Balkan, Dashhowuz and Lebap and 1992 for Turkmen-language names; Ashgabat split from Ahal around 1996 (approximate).

spans.dateNote: Statoids dates the new province names to independence (27 Oct 1991); the Russian-language articles date the velayats to 14 Dec 1992 (Balkan: oblast 1991, velayat 18 May 1992). The territory is the same either way, so one span is drawn under the oblast name.
